hypothesis: Medusa's default locking provider is in-memory, so the locks taken in acquireLockStep (per cart id) and reserveInventoryStep (per inventory item) only exclude callers inside one server process. With two servers on one database, completions racing on different servers can both read the same free WIDGET stock and both reserve it, so the run's orders need more units than were stocked (no_oversell fails, and reservations may exceed stocked quantity). Scenario: 10 WIDGET units seeded, 6 carts each wanting 2 OVS-TWOPACK (12 units total > 10), split across two servers and released together.

createReservationItems and updateReservationItems compute the new reserved_quantity from a level read before the write (MathBN.add(level.reserved_quantity, adjustment)) and write it back without a row lock or atomic increment. When two completions reserve units on the same WIDGET level at the same time, both can read the same reserved_quantity and one adjustment is overwritten, so the level's reserved_quantity ends up less than the sum of live reservations. That should fail reserved_matches_reservations. Scenario: four single-unit PIECE carts on two servers released together against the seeded WIDGET stock.

The completion workflow reads the cart and only sets completed_at much later (line ~574), so the "already completed" guard is not atomic. If the same cart is completed concurrently on two servers, the in-memory cart lock does not exclude the other process, and both completions can pass the check and each create an order for the same cart. That should fail one_order_per_cart (cart linked to two distinct orders). Scenario: one cart with one SOLO unit, completed simultaneously from both servers, several times.

The order is created by createOrdersStep and linked to the cart afterwards; if the order is saved without its cart link (or the link is written after the cart's completion response), an ok complete call would return an order id that is not linked to its cart, failing no_missing_orders. Scenario: two carts on one server completed together with a single SOLO unit each, so one succeeds and one fails, exercising the link and compensation path.

reserve-inventory.ts reserves at location_ids[0] while confirm-inventory.ts checks stock across item.location_ids. If those location lists differ for an item, stock could be confirmed at one location and reserved at another, letting the run's orders need more units than the stocked quantity at the race start. Scenario: carts prepared against the seeded WIDGET stock, then stock_before_race lowers WIDGET to 3 before completion; two-pack carts totalling more than 3 units then race.

The default locking provider is InMemoryLockingProvider, so the reservation lock keyed by WIDGET only excludes callers inside one server process. With two servers and WIDGET stock lowered to 2, one-piece carts completed simultaneously from each server can both see free stock and both reserve, so more than 2 units are promised. This is a sharper restatement of attempt 1 with a tighter stock level.
